evidence: live PG acceptance re-run attempt (R-003 / promotion gate) — did NOT pass
resolution: SUPERSEDED LATER THE SAME DAY. All four defects found here were fixed and the harness then reached L-02 passed. Success output: evidence/live-acceptance-2026-09-12.json. This file is kept as the failure history, not as the current state.
why: Boss approved re-running the live PostgreSQL acceptance to refresh the PG-endpoint TLS evidence. It was executed twice against the production DATABASE_URL (5433) with an isolated schema, and it did not pass. Both failures are recorded here rather than smoothed over.

productionSafety.mechanism: run creates a uniquely-named schema core_v0_live_<pid>_<ts>_<rand>, works only inside it, then DROPs it in cleanup
verifiedAfterwards: SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'core_v0_live%' -> empty (no leftover schema)
public table count unchanged at 44 (production tables untouched)

run1.rootCause: postgres log: ERROR: operator class "gin_trgm_ops" does not exist for access method "gin"
run1.explanation: server/memory-module-schema.sql ran `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm` while search_path held only the isolated schema. pg_trgm already exists in public, so the statement is a no-op, and the unqualified gin_trgm_ops in the index clause is then unresolvable.
run1.fix: server/memory-module-schema.sql now uses `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm SCHEMA public` and `USING gin (search_text public.gin_trgm_ops)`.
run1.rejectedFixAndWhy: Widening search_path to `<schema>, public` also makes the error go away, but public holds 44 production tables including the core_v0_* and memory_* reconciliation copies. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS would then resolve to those existing tables and the 'isolated' run would silently read and write production rows, and would report a pass. The hazard is documented in the schema file so nobody re-introduces it.

run2.note: Progress past run 1, so the schema fix worked. Fails later, in the repair/reconcile stage.
run2.diagnosis: Semantic mismatch between two in-repo components: scripts/core-v0-postgres-live-acceptance.js:667 returns `{ status: 'not_found' }` from receiptLookup when the turn admission row is absent, while server/core-v0-postgres.js:686-690 validateReceiptStatus accepts only unknown | pending | completed | failed and throws REPAIR_METADATA_INVALID otherwise.
run2.status: RESOLVED 2026-09-12 — the harness now normalises the status at its boundary (Memory vocabulary -> Core domain); L-02 passes. See evidence/live-acceptance-2026-09-12.json
options: The live harness maps an absent receipt to `unknown` (the receipt status domain stays as-is), or
The receipt status domain gains `not_found` as an authoritative answer (the harness is right and the recorder is too narrow).

configMismatchesExposed.item: L-01 is structurally unreachable in the chosen posture
configMismatchesExposed.detail: live-acceptance.js:698 requires authConfigPass = authRequired && storagePostgres && supabaseConfigured, i.e. AUTH_MODE=required plus SUPABASE_URL. This deployment deliberately uses AUTH_MODE=token (single-user personal instance), so L-01 can only ever report pending with AUTH_STORAGE_CONFIGURATION_REQUIRED.
options: Record a written waiver that the token posture covers the intent of L-01, or

configMismatchesExposed.item: The strict-TLS detector cannot see URL-form TLS configuration
configMismatchesExposed.detail: server/db-ssl.js reads only DATABASE_SSL and DATABASE_CA; it does not parse sslmode from DATABASE_URL. This deployment configures TLS as sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=... in the URL (the live connection really is strictly verified), yet the run reports strictTlsConfigured=false / sslConfiguration=configured_incomplete_or_non_strict, which would also block L-01 with STRICT_TLS_CONFIGURATION_REQUIRED.
options: Add DATABASE_SSL=true and DATABASE_CA=<repo>/.certs/prod-pg-ca.pem to .env, or
Teach the detector to honour sslmode/sslrootcert in DATABASE_URL.
